body:
# Map fleet's phase gates in PHASE_BY_GATE

Closes GitHub issue #418, and with it the ONE acceptance criterion T152 shipped unmet.

## Problem (verified, not inferred)

The fleet records its per-dispatch usage carrier and its phase gates under the gate name
`p4` (`packages/fleet/lib/live-deps.mjs` `recordDispatchUsage`, and `scheduler.mjs`'s
`effects.record('p4', ok)` reaching `adlc gate-manifest record p4`). `PHASE_BY_GATE` in
`packages/gate-manifest/lib/spend.mjs` keys on gate TOOL names from the canonical routing
table and has no `p4`/`p5` entry, so `phaseForGate('p4')` falls through to `unphased`.

Reproduce:

```
node --input-type=module -e "
import { aggregateSpend, PHASE_BY_GATE } from './packages/gate-manifest/lib/spend.mjs';
const a = aggregateSpend([{ gate: 'p4', data: { usage: { inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 20, cachedTokens: 0 } } }]);
console.log(Object.keys(a.byPhase), a.byPhase.P4, PHASE_BY_GATE.p4);"

actual:   [ 'unphased' ]  undefined  undefined
expected: [ 'P4' ]        {calls:1,...}  'P4'
```

T152 (#422) shipped the entire P4/P5 write side: usage is parsed from real harness output,
recorded exactly once per model call, enriched with routing provenance, and never
fabricated. All of it currently lands in `unphased`. So P4 — the phase ADLC.md §6 says
should be LIGHT in a healthy barbell — is precisely the phase whose spend cannot be
attributed at all, `adlc spend` under-reports P4 to zero, and the §6 `share('P4') > 0.4`
diagnostic can never fire. The instrumentation exists and reports nothing useful until this
lands.

## Why this is a separate ticket (do not repeat T152's mistake)

T152 declared `packages/gate-manifest/lib/spend.mjs` as one of its RAILS. `rail-freeze.mjs`
unions rails across all INCOMPLETE tickets, so while T152 was open that file was frozen for
EVERY pull request in the repo — including any that tried to fix this. No ceremony lifts a
ticket-declared rail: `enforceTrustRoots` states twice that ticket rails are never lifted,
and `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS` only unblocks the local editor hook, not the unbypassable
rails-guard CI diff gate. The only path was to OUTLIVE the rail — T152 completed (#424),
which expired it (T36 rails completion lifecycle). Verified empirically after that merge: an
edit to `spend.mjs` is no longer blocked by the rail hook.

**This ticket therefore declares NO rails.** A ticket must not freeze the file it exists to
change; doing so is what created the deadlock above.

## What to build

1. Add the two phase-named gates to `PHASE_BY_GATE` in
   `packages/gate-manifest/lib/spend.mjs`:

   ```
   p4: 'P4',
   p5: 'P5',
   ```

   and extend the table's doc comment to state that it accepts BOTH naming axes — gate TOOL
   names from the `/adlc:adlc` skill's routing table, and the PHASE names the fleet records
   its own per-ticket evidence under — so the lowercase entries are not later "cleaned up"
   as stray duplicates of the `P4`/`P5` values.

   Fix `p5` in the same change even though only `p4` is exercised today: it is the identical
   latent bug one line away, and fleet already records p5 verdicts.

2. Flip T152's deferred assertion. `packages/fleet/test/usage-dispatch.test.mjs` currently
   asserts only that usage reaches the RECORDER, with a header explaining that `byPhase.P4`
   cannot be asserted yet and pointing at #418. Replace that with a real
   producer-to-consumer round trip: record through the REAL gate-manifest recorder into a
   temp dir, load with the REAL loader, and assert exact `byPhase.P4` totals. Delete the
   now-obsolete deferral note rather than leaving it to rot.

Do NOT rename fleet's gate names to something like `fleet-dispatch`. Bigger, riskier, and
unnecessary: an entry the fleet recorded as its P4 phase gate genuinely IS P4 spend, so
mapping it to `P4` is honest. Checked at authoring time: the live `.adlc/manifest.jsonl`
contains ZERO entries with gate `p4` or `p5`, so no already-recorded evidence is
reinterpreted by this change — it only affects entries written from here on. Re-check before
building; if that is no longer true, the change silently re-attributes historical spend and
this ticket needs a migration note.

## Acceptance criteria

- `aggregateSpend([{gate:'p4', data:{usage:{inputTokens:100, outputTokens:20, cachedTokens:0}}}])` returns `byPhase.P4 = {calls:1, inputTokens:100, outputTokens:20, cachedTokens:0}` and NO `unphased` bucket; same for gate `p5` to `byPhase.P5`, asserting exact numbers rather than merely nonzero: verified by `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/spend.test.mjs`
- Every gate name already in `PHASE_BY_GATE` still maps to the phase it mapped to before, asserted as a WHOLE-TABLE equality against a literal expected map so a future edit cannot silently move an existing gate between phases: verified by `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/spend.test.mjs`
- An unrecognized gate name still falls through to `unphased`, preserving the staleness signal the table's own doc comment promises: verified by `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/spend.test.mjs`
- A fleet dispatch carrying parsed usage, recorded through the REAL recorder and read back through the REAL loader, aggregates to the EXACT `byPhase.P4` totals encoded in the fixture — hand-constructing manifest entries in this test is a test-integrity failure: verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/usage-dispatch.test.mjs`
- The obsolete deferral note is REMOVED, not merely amended, so the file does not keep claiming a gap that no longer exists: verified by `grep -c '#418' packages/fleet/test/usage-dispatch.test.mjs` returning 0
- Full suite green: verified by `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exiting 0

## Context

ADLC.md §6 (unit of account, barbell spend shape) and C11 ("the manifest records token spend
per phase"); issue #272 tracks the spend instrumentation gap that T152 (#422) closed the
write side of; `docs/specs/operating-stack.md` §8a is the telemetry contract. Trust-root
tier: this touches `packages/gate-manifest/`, an enforcement package, so P5 requires a
distinct-provider cross-model approve bound to the reviewed revision.
title: Map fleet's phase gates in PHASE_BY_GATE so P4 dispatch spend is attributed to P4 (closes T152's deferred criterion)
